editorial_source: Endresen, R.T., Simonsen, H.G., Sveen, A. (2000). Innføring i lingvistikk. Universitetsforlaget. Plus Læreplanverket LK20 norsk (Utdanningsdirektoratet) — kunne bokstaver, lyder, ord. The sj/kj/skj cluster inventory + æ/ø/å letters are the canonical Bokmål K-1 phonics chunk set.
policy_note: Norwegian sj-ljudet has multiple spellings (sj, skj, sk(i/e/y/æ/ø), stj) all → /ʃ/; kj-ljudet has kj, k(i/e/y/æ/ø), tj all → /ç/. The kj-sj merger (younger speakers conflate the two) is a CURRICULUM-CHOICE issue resolved by the team's locked default (treat as distinct in K-1 per traditional pedagogy; merger awareness in grade 2). The æ/ø/å letters are separate letters in their own right.

context_sensitive_chunks.comment: Context-sensitive: sk/k/g before front vowel realize as palatal/sibilant. NST gives phoneme directly so the pipeline can verify these via NST phoneme match, not by orthographic chunking.

kj_sj_merger_policy: K-1 teach kj and sj as distinct chunks per traditional Bokmål pedagogy. Grade 2: introduce awareness that younger speakers merge them. Pipeline approves both kj-words and sj-words as separate chunks; activities present them at different curriculum levels.
